endorsements.quote: Continuous monitoring should also include version control and scheduled updates of external data sources to prevent outdated or inconsistent information from influencing clinical recommendations [ 56 ].
Health care institutions must ensure that there are well-defined accountability structures in place to determine who is responsible when AI systems make errors [ 6 ].

In addition, RAG systems should be designed to provide options for clinicians to modify or override system-generated outputs when necessary, allowing for greater flexibility and ensuring that human expertise is always part of the decision-making process [ 19 54 55 ].
RAG systems should not replace human judgment but rather augment it.

Nurses and clinicians should be trained to understand the strengths and limitations of RAG systems and to intervene when they believe the AI-generated recommendation is not appropriate for the patient’s context [ 6 37 53 ].
One effective way to enhance transparency is by incorporating confidence scores and contextual explanations.
It is essential for RAG systems to explain their answers in a way that is easy for health care professionals to understand.
By continuously monitoring and correcting for bias, health care organizations can help ensure that RAG systems provide fair and equitable information support for all patients [ 43 ].
Furthermore, health care institutions and developers should also focus on including a wide range of patients in AI training data and retrieval sources to avoid making health gaps worse [ 33 34 ].
This includes defining roles and responsibilities for both human and AI components of the decision-making process.
After RAG systems are deployed in clinical practice, they must be regularly assessed for both technical accuracy and ethical impact.

unlisted_practices: Use only verified, high-quality external data sources that fit the medical context in RAG systems.
Audit RAG retrieval data sources regularly to ensure they are inclusive and reflect diverse patient demographics and clinical scenarios.
Apply fairness-aware machine learning and adversarial debiasing techniques to reduce bias in RAG-generated recommendations.
Implement a structured feedback mechanism gathering input from clinicians and affected patients to identify emerging ethical risks such as new biases, privacy concerns, or trust issues.
Ensure RAG systems meet privacy and security standards such as HIPAA and GDPR when accessing sensitive patient data.
Provide mechanisms for reporting and addressing AI errors.
Provide contextual explanations linking AI recommendations to relevant patient data or clinical guidelines.
Foster collaboration among health care professionals, AI developers, and policymakers for responsible RAG implementation.

screen.reason: This is a viewpoint article presenting strategic guidelines and ethical recommendations for implementing retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems in clinical nursing.
